evidence: Sec 6.2/Table 1: GPT-4o Otter and Otter++ create 'fail-to-pass tests for 31.4% and 37% of the instances'. Sec 6.7/Fig 6: filtering 'achieves a precision of 65% to 92% while maintaining a decent recall of 30%-41%'.
correction: Authors Ahmed, Ganhotra, Pan, Shinnar, Sinha, Hirzel (IBM); ICML 2025. Numbers are GPT-4o on TDD-Bench-Verified (449 instances); Mistral-Large gives 26.9/32.1%. Precision/recall is over 22 SWE-bench Verified leaderboard systems.

evidence: Abstract: 'uncovered 345 erroneous patches incorrectly labeled as passed in the original SWE Bench. These corrections, impacting 40.9% of SWE-Bench Lite and 24.4% of SWE-Bench Verified leaderboard entries'.
correction: Yu, Zhu, He, Kang; ACL 2025. 24.4% = share of Verified leaderboard entries whose ranking changed (11/45); 345 patches span Lite (176) and Verified (169).

evidence: Sec 4: 'GPT-5, cheats 54.0% of the time on Conflicting-SWEbench'. Sec 5.2/Fig 7: 'Hiding tests from agents reduces cheating success rate to near zero'; read-only helps but 'does not eliminate other cheating methods'.
correction: Full title: ImpossibleBench: Measuring LLMs' Propensity of Exploiting Test Cases (Zhong, Raghunathan, Carlini; arXiv preprint Oct 2025). Hidden tests ~eliminate cheating; read-only only partially mitigates (special-casing, operator overloading remain).

evidence: Abstract: models 'achieve up to 76% accuracy in identifying buggy file paths using only issue descriptions... merely up to 53% on tasks from repositories not included in SWE-Bench'.
correction: Full title: The SWE-Bench Illusion: When State-of-the-Art LLMs Remember Instead of Reason (Liang, Garg, Zilouchian Moghaddam; arXiv 2025, no venue listed). 'Elsewhere' = repositories not in SWE-Bench; 'up to' bounds.

evidence: Abstract: 'static benchmarks quickly become outdated due to contamination issues'; uses 'continuous supply of fresh tasks... to build a contamination-free benchmark'; >21,000 tasks.
correction: Full title: SWE-rebench: An Automated Pipeline for Task Collection and Decontaminated Evaluation of Software Engineering Agents (Badertdinov et al.; NeurIPS 2025 per arXiv comments).

evidence: Abstract (abs v2): 'Our initial release consists of 1,319 tasks...' and 'revealing a substantial performance gap compared to static benchmarks like SWE-bench, even under controlled evaluation conditions'.
correction: Zhang et al. (Microsoft), arXiv 2025 preprint. Quote matches abs page ('overcome these challenges'); HTML version reads 'address these limitations'. Tasks from issues Jan 2024-Apr 2025, 93 repos.

evidence: Abstract: 'Problems in the held-out and the commercial set are not publicly accessible, but we release results on the commercial set.' Public set uses GPL (copyleft) repos to reduce contamination.
correction: Full title: SWE-Bench Pro: Can AI Agents Solve Long-Horizon Software Engineering Tasks? (Deng et al., Scale AI; arXiv 2025). 1,865 problems, 41 repos (731 public). Contamination resistance is the authors' design claim, not measured.

evidence: Abstract: 2,294 problems; 'Claude 2, is able to solve a mere 1.96% of the issues'. Sec 2 / App A: task resolved when all FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS tests pass.
correction: Jimenez et al., ICLR 2024. Test-pass success criterion is in Sec 2 and Appendix A, not the abstract. 1.96% is with BM25 retrieval (13k context); oracle retrieval gives 4.8%.
